poem.content:
In the south, where sunbeams warm the ground,
A new domain unfolds, a world unbound.
I enroll my heart, a student of the earth,
Seeking relief from the weight of mortal birth.

A shift occurs, a change of pace,
As I leave behind the habits of a bygone age.
The goose that honked its warning cry,
Now leads me through the uncertain sky.

I find myself on a journey long,
With a dinosaur's spirit, strong and free to roam.
The world, a vast and wondrous oval sea,
 Beckons me to prosper, to be all I can be.

But to depend on others, to rely on their might,
Would be to lose my way, to succumb to endless night.
No, I must charge ahead, with courage as my guide,
And trust that the universe will be my ally, side by side.

In this age of wonder, where the unknown unfolds,
I'll sign my name to the page, with a heart full of gold.
For I am jelly-like, a shape-shifter, free to roam,
And in this domain, I'll find my true home.

The relief I seek, the peace I've long pursued,
Will be mine to claim, when I've learned to trust and renew.
And as I look back on the path I've trod,
I'll see the world anew, with a heart full of love and nod.
